title: Kaiserklamm Brandenberg
highlights: Spectacular gorge carved by the rushing waters of Brandenberger Ache
Historic rock-hewn trail equipped with footbridges and tunnels
Former working grounds of traditional Tyrolean log driving
Popular destination for whitewater kayakers and passionate hikers
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaiserklamm in Brandenberg thrills visitors with roaring waters, deep rocky gorges, and paths boldly carved into the cliff face.
beschreibung:
Natural Monument of Impressive Wildness

The Kaiserklamm near Brandenberg is among the most fascinating natural spectacles in Tirol. Over millennia, the untamed Brandenberger Ache carved its way deep into the hard limestone, forming a narrow gorge featuring rushing rapids, whirlpools, and sheer rock walls.

Historic Timber Floating and Secure Walkways

In former times, forestry workers used the torrential waters for dangerous log driving. Emperor Franz Joseph I visited the gorge in the 19th century, giving rise to the name Kaiserklamm. Today, a well-secured rock trail with short rock tunnels and galleries leads right alongside the roaring waters, offering captivating views into this natural jewel.
